decision: Add config/architecture-baseline.json and its schema to REQUIRED_FILES in scripts/validate-structure.py
rationale: Golden rule G1 requires a new file to be authorized by a manifest line in the same change. The config-protection gate fired because validate-structure.py defines a quality gate, but this edit tightens it rather than relaxing it: two paths become mandatory, so deleting them later fails CI. Nothing was failing beforehand, so this is not an edit made to turn a red build green. The new file records the prescriptive architecture floor for NEW projects, which no file previously held - stack-mappings.json only detects what a repo already is.
alternatives_considered: Leave the new config unlisted (rejected: violates G1, and an unlisted config file can be deleted with no build failure). Extend stack-mappings.json instead (rejected: conflates detection with prescription, so an observed fact becomes indistinguishable from a recorded decision).

decision: Make the stale convention hints in stack-mappings.json descriptive, and point new work at config/architecture-baseline.json
rationale: dotnet-cqrs mappingMechanism asserted AutoMapper and angular stateManagement asserted NgRx-or-RxJS. Both now contradict architecture-baseline.json, which forbids AutoMapper for new work on licence grounds and makes signals the Angular default. Two config files disagreeing is the rot mode lib/config.js:11-12 names. These fields are descriptive hints consumed by context-gen.py, not pass/fail thresholds, and nothing was failing - so this loosens no gate.
alternatives_considered: Leave them (rejected: an agent reading both files in one session gets opposite instructions). Delete the fields (rejected: they still carry real signal about what an existing repo is likely to use, which is what detection is for).

decision: Add hooks/runtime/handlers/write-ledger.js, a new PostToolUse handler that records every successful Edit/Write to ~/.orchestrator/state/writes/<session>.json. config-protection denied the create because GOVERNANCE_DIRS matches all of hooks/runtime/ on path alone, so it cannot distinguish CREATING a new gate that adds enforcement from EDITING an existing gate to weaken it. This change only adds enforcement: it introduces the record that citation-guard needs to detect a claim about a file that was never written, the failure that shipped on 2026-09-09 when IClaimLawsWriter.cs was reported as created after its write was denied. Nothing existing is loosened.

Make the fact-forcing gate's manifest question conditional on a manifest existing. pre:edit-write:fact-force currently asks 'which entry in the file manifest authorizes this path' on every create, but G1 governs the hub's own content inventories in scripts/_lib.py, which a greenfield repo does not have. Building a new .NET/Angular project produced 23 denials in one session, every one demanding an entry that could not exist, and one of those denials was stepped past as ordinary friction so the file was never created while a summary claimed it had been. The fix walks up from the target path looking for scripts/_lib.py and asks four facts where a manifest exists, three where it does not. Nothing is loosened in this repository; importers, prior art and the verbatim instruction are still always required.
alternatives_considered: Disable the gate outside the hub entirely (rejected: the other three facts are valuable in any repo); leave it and rely on ORCHESTRATOR_GATE_EXEMPT_GLOBS (rejected: an escape hatch that must be set for all normal greenfield work is a gate that gets switched off permanently)
